title: Colour elements by a parameter with a rule-based view filter
task: Create a rule-based ParameterFilterElement over a category (rule from ParameterFilterRuleFactory), add it to a view and override its graphics (e.g. red projection lines) with View.SetFilterOverrides and OverrideGraphicSettings. Covers rule-based view filters and graphic overrides for QA and standards.

pitfalls.symptom: ParameterFilterElement.Create throws ArgumentException 'One of the given rules refers to a parameter that does not apply to this filter's categories'.
pitfalls.cause: The rule's parameter must be one of the categories' filterable parameters, not any parameter.
pitfalls.fix: Pick the rule parameter from ParameterFilterUtilities.GetFilterableParametersInCommon(doc, categories), or use a broadly-filterable instance parameter like ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS.

pitfalls.symptom: View.SetFilterOverrides has no visible effect on the view.
pitfalls.cause: The view's Filters are controlled by its view template, so filter edits on the view itself are ignored.
pitfalls.fix: Apply filters to a view with no template (View.ViewTemplateId == ElementId.InvalidElementId), or add the filter to the template instead.

pitfalls.symptom: A task-phrased search like 'create a rule-based parameter filter and override element color' surfaces the ParameterFilterRuleFactory rules but not ParameterFilterElement.Create or View.SetFilterOverrides.
pitfalls.cause: The filter-create and override-apply members rank below the rule factory for filter intent (connector issue #341 family).
pitfalls.fix: The rule factory is the anchor; from a FilterRule, wrap it in ElementParameterFilter, build the filter with ParameterFilterElement.Create, and apply graphics with View.SetFilterOverrides(filterId, OverrideGraphicSettings).

miss.text: create a rule-based parameter filter and override element color and lineweight in a view
